insights: An urgent planner option that a reflex will cancel right away does harm. It breaks off the current fight, so planner conditions must match the reflex thresholds such as reflex.melee_dist.

A skill's refusal checks must accept everything its reflex caller can hand it (reflex.melee_dist vs a hardcoded 4-block cutoff), or the reflex starts a skill that fails at once while the threat stays on us.
A progress detector keyed only on position punishes skills whose real progress is gathering items in place; check the skill's actual output before declaring stuck.
build_portal NO_ROOM failed instantly on retries because the carve fallback only tested a single room layout anchored at the bot's feet, and next to a lava pool that layout always touches the lava.

At the ocean the remembered water sources had no dry bank, so fill_bucket failed NOT_FOUND while explore water said ALREADY_DONE; a refusing skill needs the fallback a player would use (scoop from where you stand) or the planner loops between two refusals.
A retreat that starts with a monster 3-4 blocks away can't get away: the mob follows and hits our back. Fleeing only makes sense past melee range, or when we can wall in on the spot.

A reflex that checks only distance keeps restarting a fight the planner has already given up on (unreachable mark). The reflex's trigger should honour the same unreachable memory, with an exception for a mob that is really in reach.

When the planner's inventory test (Goal.have bucket counts filled buckets) says a step is ready but the skill's own check refuses, the skill must fix the state itself (pour out the spare water), or the planner offers the same refused step forever.

Creeper HAZARD failures happened because the attack quit as soon as it saw a lit fuse. The follow-up retreat then started 2-3 blocks from the creeper and failed with NO_PROGRESS, so backing off at once inside the attack should beat handing over to a new skill.

Repeated shore TIMEOUTs come from a 90 s pathed swim that doesn't move the bot. After one failure, swimming by hand on the surface toward seen land (or straight ahead), and switching targets when it stalls, should beat trying the same route again.

When a skill's special method needs room the spot lacks, a fallback that uses the visible resource as it stands (mine the world's gravel) should beat repeating the refusal while explore says the target is already seen.

Shore TIMEOUTs repeat because the pathed swim keeps going to the same unreachable land. Swimming by hand with a stall check every 5 s, which drops the stalled target or turns, should keep the bot moving instead of spending another 90 s in place.

When two planner phases choose the same kind of step by different rules (the furnace batch already cooking vs the largest raw stack), they swap each other's choice on every decision; give them one shared rule.
The shelter exit failed because StairUp needed a block to fill a step; a climb-out that pillars when it has blocks and otherwise digs a step staircase needs no placements to succeed.

A seen-only collect that instantly refuses lets the planner hand the same refusal back over and over; folding the search into the skill (as stoneStep does with stairs) turns a 3 s fail loop into progress.

collect log NOT_FOUND repeats because collect only looks 3 s within 64 blocks while explore log says ALREADY_DONE for logs seen further away; a step that closes that gap until collect's own check passes should end the two-refusal loop.

fortress find UNREACHABLE repeated back to back because each failed leg ended the skill and the planner offered the same step again. Turning to a new heading inside the skill should be cheaper than a full re-decision and a new pie-chart sweep each time.
Shore STUCK is the pathed swim pinned against a bank it can't jump onto; offering on just lastSkill=shore+STUCK while main is shore (no extra preconditions) makes sure the fallback actually runs.
A fallback explore whose target is already in view can never succeed. Retarget it to new ground so the step it backs up gets a fresh place to try, rather than repeating two instant refusals.

Repeated collect STUCK happens at a spot Baritone can't path out of, and unstuck's walk barely moves the bot, so the retry stalls again. A hand-driven dig-and-walk that must reach 3 blocks of real displacement should give the next collect a new start.
A failure mark has to cover every way a skill picks its direction: the bad-heading mark only fed exploreHeading, so the pie-chart sweep could keep choosing the heading that had just failed.
An upkeep step that pays off in one dimension (cave torches) can quietly use up a large share of time in another dimension where it does little, so gate upkeep steps by the dimension where they help.

attack creeper HAZARD fires whenever the single straight-back step is unsafe; widening the escape to diagonal backsteps should keep the bot outrunning the blast in cramped terrain instead of losing time in a handoff.

The staircase climb fails on hard blocks, side hazards and slow 240 s timeouts; a vertical pillar that feeds on its own mined cobble needs only one clear column and sidesteps when that column is blocked.

attack creeper HAZARD mostly fires on an unlit creeper after the backing walk stalls; failing there only hands control to retreat (the top action before deaths), so the HAZARD bail-out should be kept for a lit fuse only.

The log loop comes from explore trusting remembered blocks that collect has just shown it can't use. Tying explore's 'already seen' check to collect's latest NOT_FOUND should make explore move instead of refusing.

Lava is the top cause of first-life deaths in the Nether, and 13 of those deaths came while attacking a magma cube or hoglin. In-fight movement that matters little on the overworld (jumps, strafes) can be what kills the bot beside lava, so gate footwork by dimension.
explore any UNREACHABLE repeats back-to-back because each blocked heading ends the skill; turning to a fresh heading within the skill should convert those instant failures into actual exploration.

The planner and the skills must judge from the same up-to-date view: a view up to 5 ticks old (and not updated at all while dead) makes the first decisions after a respawn chase mobs that are no longer in sight.

When the bot is already out at sea, turning back after 20 s of swimming and marking that heading bad makes every explore leg a short loop. An explore leg that starts in water should keep going in a straight line to land and then hand back to shore.

Backing up while facing a creeper is no faster than the creeper walks, so the gap never opens. Turning away and sprinting is the only player movement that actually outruns it, and the attack should do that itself instead of failing over to retreat.

The 'climbed 0 blocks' STUCK message means the pillar jumped for 20 s without placing a block. A likely cause is too little headroom: a jump needs about 3 free blocks above the feet, and only the block 2 up was cleared.

Blazes keep spawning across a fortress and at its spawner. Running out of untried anchors only means the bot has to wait somewhere, so failing hands the fight back to a planner that just restarts it in the same place.

blazes NOT_FOUND means the known part of the fortress is exhausted, not the fortress; since fortress find refuses once any brick is known, the fight itself must extend what is known by walking beyond its edge.

Attack UNREACHABLE mostly fires at 3-4 blocks when the pathfinder's 'near' goal stalls on a ledge, hole or water; direct key movement toward a visible mob can close that last gap where pathing gives up.

The tried-anchor exclusion is a 20-block disc around both the anchor and the bot's own spot. That uses up a partly seen fortress in about 4 hops, before the 2-minute retry reopens anything. A smaller radius gets the fight more anchors without adding new walking logic.
Most Nether first deaths (lava, onFire, inFire) come during fortress:blazes from near-full health, so they are sudden environmental deaths; where the chase leads matters more than when the bot heals.

Nether fortress deaths are sudden hits (lava, fire, piglins) that land while the bot is chasing. The one cheap thing the bot controls is starting every fortress leg at full health instead of the median 16, because health only regenerates at 18+ hunger and only while the bot stands still and safe.

Creeper HAZARD failures happen when the back-off stalls while the creeper is still harmless (not swelling); handing over to retreat is where the deaths happen, so the attack should keep hitting until the fuse actually lights.
When two skills hand off to each other, they must use the same 'seen' range. If collect only counts logs within 64 blocks and explore counts any seen log, the two fail back and forth forever.

Nether first deaths come from near-full health (piglin, wither skeleton, fireball knockback into lava). Earlier attempts changed where the bot fights, and all of them lost. This one changes how it fights: keeping the guard up between swings.
Skills that set up the hand or camera only once in start() can be undone by per-tick code (lighting, guard) that runs before them; eat should re-check its preconditions every tick.

An explore that times out on a 120-block path toward one spot gets better odds from a short sideways walk by keys that stops when an animal comes into view than from a long path in the same direction.
A skill that fails the same way repeatedly in one spot (flint NO_ROOM 55x back-to-back) needs a different method on retry, not the same one again.
Retreat is the last choice before most first deaths and arrows are the top killer, so running from ranged mobs on open ground hands them free shots; closing in with the shield up should do better.

The planner only reacts to Nether monsters within 4 blocks, so any retreat it starts there begins at arm's length among lava and drops and rarely gets away; fighting back is likely the better default there.
Skip an option when what the player can see already says it will fail (vanilla's no-sleep-with-monsters-within-8 rule); this beats letting the skill time out and get offered again.
A skill that fails NO_ROOM where it stands should move to open ground before it starts, not change how it gets the item after failing (in-place gravel mining lost in g327).
The blaze fight runs out of anchors because a 20-block tried radius soon covers every brick it has seen. It needs a way to see more of the fortress, not another try at the same spots.
Retreat NO_PROGRESS at 3 blocks comes from Baritone giving up on GoalRunAway, not from the decision to flee; changing the decision lost repeatedly, so fix how the escape moves.

Nether first deaths (piglin 14, wither skeleton 9) mostly happen during fortress:blazes, which blocks all re-planning, so the bot never answered melee attackers there; letting close melee threats through tests whether that blind spot is the killer.

When a fortress run times out, retrying from the same spot repeats the timeout; the bot should first move to a different part of the fortress it has seen (or look around), then hand back to the fortress skill.
Flint NO_ROOM repeats back-to-back in one spot, so the retry should switch to a method that needs no free spot beside us (mining seen gravel) instead of walking elsewhere or retrying the same steps.
Blazes only spawn at the spawner, so when the fight runs out of anchors, returning to the known spawner should beat walking toward unseen floors (g363) or giving up NOT_FOUND.

Flint NO_ROOM repeats in tight underground spots. Walking to open ground and mining seen gravel both lost, so this tries making the room in place by digging one side cell, a few seconds of work, then hands back to the normal flint steps.

At the nether frontier, the worst run lost its whole time to enter_portal being cut short over and over by mob decisions. Going through the portal also gets away from overworld mobs, so finishing the trip should beat fighting near it.

Flint NO_ROOM may come from where flint gets offered (side work in a cramped mine) rather than from the flint skill's steps. Earlier fixes changed the skill after it failed and all lost; this one changes when the planner offers it.

Shore TIMEOUT repeats up to seven times in a row in the same water, so retrying the same pathfinder route doesn't work; the follow-up should move a different way (direct key swimming) and stop going for a target once it stops getting closer.
